_notes: Power-up (about 18:30) to curtain at 19:30 - roughly 45-60 minutes, so about 15 cycles of a ~210s loop. Anchors carry the production; wildcards rotate through three groups so a Lovett slide, a penny-dreadful fact and a Criterion message each recur in turn rather than three adverts in a row. Every trivia slide carries its own item.content - see docs/cascade-prompts/2026-08-per-item-slide-content.md. ALL COPY IS DRAFT pending Boondog approval: docs/lovett-copy-for-approval.md.

items._note: House-open one-shot, slide 1 of 2 - the fuller advisory for people arriving and deciding. The rolling warning-top3 anchor carries the headline three all evening. Matches the Popcorn pattern (P05 split).
Slide 2 of 2. Ends on no-interval, which is the practical one people act on.

about-ben is the generic 'about the writer' template despite its Popcorn-era name - it reads show.foyer_content.writer. Lucy wrote and performs Lovett, so this is the right slide. The `cast` template is a two-column role/actor table, which is a thin slide for a one-woman show.

content.headline: Born in a penny dreadful
content.body: Sweeney Todd and Mrs Lovett first appeared in The String of Pearls (1846-47) - a serialised "penny dreadful", lurid fiction sold at a penny an issue.

items._note: The plate's masthead and cartouche are typeset in Rye and IM Fell English, so this one wants the large feature treatment rather than a poster frame.

content.headline: A whaler's daughter
content.body: A whaler father, a courtesan mother, a butcher husband. Everything Eleanor knows how to do, she learned from someone else's trade.

content.headline: It opens in darkness
content.body: The first thing you will hear tonight is a knife being drawn across a whetstone.

content.headline: Why pies?
content.body: Victorians had good reason to fear a cheap pie. Food adulteration was rife in 1840s London and "mystery meat" was a genuine public scandal. The legend fed on a real fear.

content.headline: Nellie is short for Eleanor
content.body: Sondheim called her Nellie Lovett. Tonight's Eleanor is the woman before the legend.

content.headline: She's been here before
content.body: Lovett previewed at the Belgrade, just down the road, in July 2025 - before its Edinburgh premiere. Tonight she's back in Coventry.

content.headline: Not booked? Ask at the desk
content.body: Tickets are usually available on the door right up to curtain-up. Front-of-house will tell you what's left.

items._note: Replaces the tickets-walkins template, which hard-codes Popcorn magenta and Anton INLINE in slide-templates.js and assumes the Criterion's member/non-member/under-25 price bands - neither of which fits a visiting production. See docs/backlog/foyer-templates-popcorn-hardcoding.md.

Popcorn ran the volunteer call in preshow as well as postshow; Lovett had it only in postshow. A visiting-company night brings in people who have never been to the Criterion before, so preshow is arguably where it matters most.
